profiles.name: Plausible Analytics
profiles.why: Plausible's pricing page lists a Starter plan at $9/month for one site at the 10k-monthly-pageview tier, while Simple Analytics's self-serve plan starts at €20/month including 1 user (E13); the figures are in different currencies and cover different allowances, so this shows Plausible's named entry price is numerically smaller, not a currency-adjusted discount. Both build their pitch around non-personal, cookie-free tracking: Plausible's homepage says 'No cookies, no persistent identifiers, no cross-site or cross-device tracking,' and Simple Analytics's pricing page states it 'only processes non-personal data' to satisfy GDPR, the ePrivacy Directive, the UK GDPR, and the PECR (E19).
profiles.discovery_reason: The first name that comes up when searching for a lightweight, cookie-free alternative to Google Analytics, and it undercuts Simple Analytics on price for a single site.
profiles.one_liner: Easy to use and privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative
profiles.promise: Plausible gives you clear, useful insights without complexity, training or prior analytics experience.
profiles.pricing: Usage-tiered by monthly pageviews across four plans: Starter $9/month (one site, 10k-pageview tier shown), Growth $14/month (up to 3 sites/3 team members, same tier), Business $19/month (up to 10 sites/10 team members, Stats API at 600 req/hr, same tier), Enterprise custom via sales (10+ sites, 10+ team members, SSO, managed proxy); annual billing gives 2 months free; prices shown are for the lowest displayed pageview tier and scale up with volume.
profiles.free_entry: 30-day free trial on any plan, no credit card required; open-source codebase ('our code is open source too, so you're never locked in').
profiles.icp: 'Most site owners' for whom Google Analytics is overkill; the homepage also cites 'thousands of organizations' and docs cite '22,000+ teams'.
profiles.note: 4 claim(s) the extractor reported were not on their pages and were discarded

rivals.name: Plausible Analytics
rivals.why: The first name that comes up when searching for a lightweight, cookie-free alternative to Google Analytics, and it undercuts Simple Analytics on price for a single site.

rivals.name: Fathom Analytics
rivals.why: Pitched as the simplest dashboard of the privacy-first tools and flat-priced across unlimited sites, so agencies managing several client sites compare it directly against Simple Analytics.

rivals.name: Matomo
rivals.why: The self-hosted option for a buyer who wants full data control and deeper reports instead of accepting Simple Analytics' deliberately minimal, hosted-only metrics.

rivals.name: Google Analytics (GA4)
rivals.why: What the buyer almost certainly already has installed via a consent banner and Consent Mode, and the thing Simple Analytics is pitched to run alongside or replace because consent rejections hide 20-60% of traffic from it.

rivals.name: Umami
rivals.why: The free, open-source script a developer on the team spins up and self-hosts instead of paying a monthly SaaS fee for Simple Analytics.
